geo.summary_lead: Summary: Increase Volume (App Store title "Increase Volume Sound") is an iPhone app that processes audio and video files on the device, applies up to 10× volume multiplication with an optional audio-quality enhancement, and saves a new, louder file you can keep or share. It does not raise the iPhone speaker's hardware limit for system-wide sound.
geo.summary_body: Published on the Apple App Store by Vladimir Ivakhnenko (c-basso) in the Music and Utilities categories. It solves the same problem as normalizing or amplifying audio in iMovie, Audacity or an online booster, but as a one-slider workflow on iPhone that also handles plain audio files, not only video.

faq.question: How do I make a video louder on iPhone?
faq.answer: Open Increase Volume, import the video from Photos (or share it to the app), drag the Volume multiplication slider up to ×10, tap Boost Volume, compare Original and Processed, then tap Download Processed. The louder copy lands in Photos or Files and plays loud on every device.

faq.question: Can I make a voice memo louder after recording it?
faq.answer: Yes. Share the memo from Voice Memos to Increase Volume (or save it to Files first), boost it up to ×10, and save the processed file. Voice Memos' own Enhance Recording only cleans noise during playback; it does not create a louder file.

faq.question: Does Increase Volume work on MP3 and other audio files, not just video?
faq.answer: Yes. It boosts MP3, M4A and other common audio files as well as MP4 and MOV videos. Most iPhone volume booster apps only accept video; this one is listed as an Audio & Music Booster and shows the track name, size and duration before you boost.

faq.question: Why is my iPhone screen recording so quiet?
faq.answer: iOS captures app audio at a conservative level, and Bluetooth headphones or a low in-app volume make it quieter still. You cannot fix a finished recording with system settings, but Increase Volume can multiply its audio up to ×10 and save a new file.

faq.question: Will boosting the volume make my video sound distorted?
faq.answer: Only if you push a recording that is already near its ceiling. Start around ×3 to ×5, use the Original/Processed toggle to listen before saving, and switch on Improve Audio Quality for speech. Quiet sources usually take ×5 to ×10 cleanly.

faq.question: How much louder than iMovie can it go?
faq.answer: iMovie on iPhone caps clip volume at roughly 500%. Increase Volume goes to ×10 (1000%), works without building a project, and also accepts audio-only files that iMovie cannot open.

faq.question: Can I boost a video straight from the Photos app?
faq.answer: Yes. Open the video in Photos, tap Share, choose Increase Volume, and a project is created instantly. Boost it, then Download Processed to save the louder copy back to Photos.

faq.question: Does Increase Volume make my iPhone speaker louder?
faq.answer: No. It makes the audio inside a file louder and saves a new copy. If a recording is too quiet even at maximum system volume, boosting the file is the fix; the app cannot change the speaker's hardware limit or system-wide volume.

faq.question: Is Increase Volume free? What does the subscription unlock?
faq.answer: The download is free and includes a free trial. Continued unlimited boosting is unlocked with a subscription or a one-time lifetime plan; current prices are shown on the App Store listing. Processing always happens on your iPhone.

faq.question: Is my audio uploaded anywhere?
faq.answer: No. The boost is computed on your iPhone and the result is saved locally through the standard iOS share sheet. There is no account and no server-side processing step.
